title: \textbf{The Chain Atom $W=u^5v+v^6$, the Missing Leading Term $v^{11

claims.statement: For $W = u^5v + v^6$ with exponent matrix $A = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}5 & 1\\ 0 & 6\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ and transpose $W^T = u^5 + uv^6$ with $A^T = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}5 & 0\\ 1 & 6\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$: • $|\det A| = |\det A^T| = |\mathrm{Aut}(W)| = |\mathrm{Aut}(W^T)| = 30$, and central charge $\hat{c}(W) = \hat{c}(W^T) = 4/3$. • $\mu(W) = (6-1)^2 = 25$, whereas $W^T$ is quasihomogeneous of weights $(3,2)$ and degree $15$ with $\mu(W^T) = (15/3 - 1)(15/2 - 1) = 26$. • In $\mathbb{C}[u,v]/(\partial W^T)$ where $\partial_u W^T = 5u^4 + v^6$ and $\partial_v W^T = 6uv^5$, the relation $v^6 \equiv -5u^4$ implies $v^{12} \equiv 25u^8$ and $u v^5 = 0 \implies v^{11} = v^5(-5u^4) = -5u^3(uv^5) \equiv 0$, cutting the monomial box at $v^{11}$ to yield dimension $26$.
claims.title: Chain Atom vs.\ Berglund--H\"ubsch Transpose
